sources.title: Realty Transfer Fee
sources.use: Current standard and partial-exemption schedules, covered property classes, statutory responsibility, and graduated percentage bands.
sources.limit: The page cannot determine a deed's consideration, classification, exemption, recording date, or transaction-specific amount.

sources.title: Amendments to Graduated Percent Fee on Realty Transfers over $1 Million
sources.use: Confirms the July 10, 2025 effective date, seller responsibility, straight percentage of total consideration, and five current percentage bands.
sources.limit: The transition refund provision described in the notice is historical and is not calculated by this tool.

sources.publisher: New Jersey Department of Banking and Insurance
sources.title: Bulletin 24-11: Real Estate Brokerage Business Relationships
sources.use: Current state guidance on written brokerage services agreements, compensation negotiability, permitted payors, and agency disclosures.
sources.limit: It does not replace a consumer's signed agreement or transaction-specific legal advice.

sources.title: Real Estate Frequently Asked Questions
sources.use: Supports the distinction between the Consumer Information Statement and a separate agreement establishing an agency relationship.
sources.limit: The regulator FAQ is general guidance and does not decide a consumer's contract terms.

sources.publisher: New Jersey Department of Banking and Insurance
sources.title: Consumer Information: Real Estate
sources.use: Official state directory for real-estate consumer guidance and Commission materials.
sources.limit: The directory does not determine contract, inspection, title, lending, or closing outcomes.

sources.publisher: New Jersey Department of Banking and Insurance
sources.title: Everything You Wanted to Know About Buying a Home
sources.use: Supports the limited New Jersey statement that many buyers retain attorneys although doing so is not required, plus general contract, inspection, and title concepts.
sources.limit: The publication contains legacy federal-form references, so current mortgage disclosures are sourced separately from CFPB.

sources.title: Loan Estimate Explainer
sources.use: Current federal consumer guidance for comparing estimated loan terms and closing costs in covered mortgage transactions.
sources.limit: A Loan Estimate is not final approval, a title report, or a promise that a transaction will close.

sources.title: Closing Disclosure Explainer
sources.use: Current federal guidance for reviewing final loan terms and costs in the Closing Disclosure for covered mortgages.
sources.limit: The disclosure does not establish a universal New Jersey closing timetable or resolve contract and title issues.

sources.title: Local Property Tax
sources.use: Official starting point for New Jersey assessment, billing, county-board, and property-tax resources.
sources.limit: A statewide page cannot state a parcel's assessment, rate, bill, appeal result, or relief eligibility.

sources.publisher: New Jersey Department of Community Affairs
sources.title: Housing Discrimination
sources.use: Official New Jersey fair-housing information and complaint resources.
sources.limit: The page is general public information and does not decide whether particular conduct violated the law.

sources.title: Monthly Housing Market Statistics
sources.use: Current public statewide and county housing-market reports and their monthly update cadence.
sources.limit: Municipality reports require member access; this guide does not copy or invent local figures or predict future prices.

sources.title: Statistical Information
sources.use: Official annual assessment, property-tax, and residential-sales files with year-specific columns and completion limits.
sources.limit: Annual statewide files are not live listing data and an incomplete year's blank columns must not be treated as current sales results.

sources.title: Consider whether it is the right time for you to buy
sources.use: Consumer framework for testing target-area prices, rent-versus-buy assumptions, moving horizon, income stability, ownership risks, and repairs.
sources.limit: The guidance does not forecast the New Jersey market or decide whether an individual should buy, sell, rent, or wait.

sources.title: How can I figure out if I can afford to buy a home and take out a mortgage?
sources.use: Supports a personal-budget test based on income, expenses, savings priorities, insurance, and ownership costs rather than only a lender qualification amount.
sources.limit: It is general consumer education, not mortgage approval, financial advice, or a property-specific affordability conclusion.

gscEvidence.period: Last 3 months in the exported Pages comparison reviewed 2026-08-26
